{{figure:fig_7_1.webp}}

The diagram shows the graph of the probability density function, f, of a random variable $X$ which takes values between −3 and 2 only.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Given that the graph is symmetrical about the line $x = -0.5$ and that $\text{P}(X < 0) = p$, find $\text{P}(-1 < X < 0)$ in terms of $p$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
It is now given that the probability density function shown in the diagram is given by

$$\text{f}(x) = \begin{cases} a - b(x^2 + x) & -3 \leqslant x \leqslant 2, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases}$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: By substituting a suitable value of $x$ into $\text{f}(x)$, find another equation relating $a$ and $b$ and hence determine the values of $a$ and $b$.
